chapman_cardiff.text: Chapbooks! Bilingual on request, shouty on Saturdays. Which move are you after?

rail_guard.text: Cardiff Central. Rugby fans on the left, shoppers on the right, everybody in the way.
Hop aboard. The Wildlore rail runs to any town you have visited. Where to?

then.text: Lovely hooped shirt. You either know your rugby or you know your mud.
Dydd Gŵyl Dewi Hapus! Happy St David's Day. Daffodil in the lapel, leek in the bag, Welsh cakes in the gob.
All I want for Christmas is a Grand Slam. Failing that, socks.
Autumn internationals! Red from the castle to the Bay. Then we lose to someone and it's red from crying.
Rain, is it? Proper rugby weather, that. Slippery ball, muddy knees, loud singing.
Wind's blowing a hooley across the Taff. I'd not want to be kicking for goal today.
Floodlights coming on at the stadium. Best sight in Cardiff, that. After a Welsh cake.

rugby_fan.text: {greeting} I'd tell you the score but it changes every time I get a hot dog.
The Principality Stadium holds seventy-four thousand and they all sing at once. Hearing it from outside is free.

then.text: Rain on the castle walls. The peacocks have gone indoors to file a complaint.
Fog round the keep! Very spooky. We'll pretend it's planned. Atmosphere, see.

castle_guide2.text: Cardiff Castle has a Roman wall at its foot and a Victorian fairy-tale on top. Two thousand years in one view.
The peacocks on the lawn are not decorative. They're managers.

bay_sailor.text: Cardiff Bay used to be the biggest coal port on the planet. In 1913 more coal left here than any other port in the world.
Now it's mostly ferries, ice creams and people photographing the same bollard.

then.text: Drizzle again. Roald Dahl would've invented a word for this. Something like 'splishsplodgy'.
Early start for lectures. Cardiff's lovely at dawn. I'll be fully awake now in a minute.

dahl_fan.text: Roald Dahl was born in Cardiff. He's the reason I check every sweet shop for a golden ticket.
They've named a plaza after him. No giant peaches, but the water tower is quite tall.

then.text: Sent my little one to school dressed as a daffodil. She's been photosynthesising all morning.
Costume shopping. My husband wants to go as a dragon. I said, you already snore like one.
Came into town for wrapping paper. Leaving with a reindeer jumper for the dog. Classic Queen Street.
Raining again, cariad. To the arcades! I'll be in and out now in a minute. Well, an hour. Two.
Sun's out! Nobody knows what to do. We've all brought umbrellas out of habit.

shopper.text: {greeting} Cardiff's Victorian arcades are the best shopping you can do in the rain. Which is to say, all of it.
I came in for a coat. I left with three hats and a bag of Welsh cakes. A win.

then.text: I'm not streaming for a while. I'm trying a new hobby called 'looking at the sea'.
It's very good. You don't get comments. Not even from the seagulls.

else.text: Oh, it's you. I thought it would be, honestly.

then.text: {player}. Cardiff Bay, no cameras. I switched them off. That should tell you something.
I've seen what the Enclosure actually does. The free merch was a lot less free than it looked.
I'm done with the sponsorship. But I'm not done with you. Let's go!

else.text: I mean it, about the Enclosure. I've sent them an email. A long one. It had a heading in bold.
I'll still be around. And I'm going to beat you one day. On camera. Possibly with a banner.
Go on. Pryce and Rhys are about. Rhys is the Keeper. Pryce is the other one.

pryce_cardiff.text: Ah. Cardiff. Our offices are just up there, the glass ones. You may have seen the sign. It says 'Synergy'.
I have reviewed Llanberis. I have reviewed Yr Wyddfa. Overall performance: below target. I attribute this to you.
Today I am restructuring you. Out of the Stones, and into the history books. Politely, of course.
I note the outcome. I note it for the record. I note it in a very small font.
The Cardiff office will be closing for the foreseeable. For team building. In Swindon.
Pryce walks off towards the glass offices, looking like a man who has been audited by a dragon.

cardiff_east_gate.text: Severn road's closed, I'm afraid. Enclosure survey of the bridge. We're counting the cables. It's going slowly.
Come back when you've got the Storm Stone. Keeper Rhys says we're not to let anyone leave Cardiff without a proper soaking.

cardiff_night_nurse.text: Off to the Heath hospital for the night shift, cariad. Somebody has to keep Cardiff ticking while it sleeps.
Quiet streets, a full flask and a bag of Welsh cakes. That's a night nurse's toolkit, that is.
Mind yourself out here at this hour. The Bay's lovely at night, but it's a long walk back.

cardiff_fox_watcher.text: There's a fox family living by Bute Park. They come out when the city goes to bed.
Red torch, see. Foxes don't mind it. They just sit there looking at me like I'm the odd one.

then.text: Diolch, and mahadsanid. That's thank you in Welsh and in Somali. In Butetown you get both.
He gave you the biscuits? He likes you, then.
Here. A lump of Welsh steam coal, polished. It's what brought everyone here, in the end. Keep it in your pocket and remember the stokers.

else.text: The Tiger Bay plaque, then Mr Saleh. He'll be the one with the flat cap and the opinions.
The Tiger Bay plaque, then Mr Saleh. He'll be the one with the flat cap and the opinions.
{greeting} Shwmae! I'm Amina. My great-grandad came to Cardiff from Somaliland as a ship's fireman, shovelling coal in the stokehold. Hottest job at sea, he said, and he'd know.
Butetown has had Somali and Yemeni families for more than a hundred years. We're as Cardiff as the castle. Older than some of it, actually.
Learn about Tiger Bay with Amina?

then.text: Go and read the Tiger Bay plaque, then find Mr Saleh. Everyone calls him Grandad. He'll tell you about the Yemeni side, at length, with biscuits.

isles_saleh.text: {greeting} Saleh. My father came from Aden, in Yemen, on the coal boats in the 1930s, and married a girl from Splott. Her mam nearly fainted. Then she learnt to make his coffee and wouldn't let anyone else touch the pot.
Yemeni sailors opened boarding houses here, and cafes, and a place to pray. Our lot have been part of this city since before your grandparents were born.
We kept Ramadan, we cheered for Wales, and we argued about Cardiff City. Faith is one thing. Football is serious.

then.text: Amina sent you? Tell her the biscuits are better at mine. Here, have one. Have two.
